---
title: Source
---

## Overview

A **source** retrieves documents. A **tool** exposes an action to the model. Keeping them separate allows the same Elasticsearch, web, or file source to support search visit, or a custom tool interface.

Built-in tools include `search`, `visit`, and `mcp`.

## Configure Tools

Tools are configured with the `source` they operate on, and `name`, `description`, and `inputSchema` which are exposed to LLM for tool call.

```yaml
agent:
  tools:
  - type: search
      name: search
      description: Search for more information.
      inputSchema: # input schema
      source:
        - elasticsearch
  - type: visit
      name: visit
      description: Fetch full text with document id
      inputSchema: # input schema
      source:
        - file_1
```

## Customize the tool informations provided to model

Tool behavior and model-facing presentation are configured independently:

```yaml
agent:
  tools:
    - type: search
      name: search_web
      description: Search the indexed web corpus for evidence.
      source: [corpus]
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        properties:
          key_word:
            type: string
            description: A focused search query.
        required: [key_word]
        additionalProperties: false
      argument_mapping:
        key_word: query
      raise_argument_validation_error: false
```

`argument_mapping` can rename model-visible arguments before execution. Keep schemas small and unambiguous: the model should see only arguments it can use correctly.

## Summarize large tool results

Search and visit tools can pass their output through a separate summarizer model:

```yaml
agent:
  tools:
    - type: visit
      name: visit
      source: [corpus]
      summary_goal_key: goal
      summarizer:
        model: Qwen3-8B
        base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8010/v1
        api_key: EMPTY
        max_chars: 40000
        max_concurrency: 128
        default_kwargs:
          max_tokens: 1024
        retry_config:
          max_tries: 3
```

The summarizer reduces context growth but adds latency and another failure surface.
Use it when raw documents are substantially larger than the evidence needed.

## MCP tools

Use `type: mcp` to expose a tool hosted by an MCP server. Configure the server
transport and remote tool name in the `ToolConfig` fields used by `MCPTool`. MCP tools
share the same initialization, validation, retry, and shutdown lifecycle as native
tools.

For custom retrieval, subclass `DataSource` and use `type: custom` with a `target`.
For custom model actions, subclass `BaseTool` and register the implementation with
`register_tool()` before building the agent.

For complete examples of defining and configuring these extensions, see
[Custom modules](../04-advanced-usage/01-custom-modules.qmd)
